import SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsBook

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open Set
open scoped Matrix BigOperators

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsResidualWeightingIdentification27
open CompleteFoundationsSpectralModels (E point norm_squared_coordinates)

def rectangularH : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 2) ℝ := !![1,1;1,11/10;0,1]
def noisyY : Fin 3 → ℝ := ![6,31/5,21/10]
def actualResidual (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (rectangularH *ᵥ z-noisyY)

theorem actual_rectangular_columns_are_independent : Function.Injective rectangularH.mulVec := by
  intro x y h
  have h0 := congrArg (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ => z 0) h
  have h2 := congrArg (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ => z 2) h
  simp [rectangularH,Matrix.mulVec,dotProduct,Fin.sum_univ_succ] at h0 h2
  ext i
  fin_cases i
  · change x 0=y 0
    linarith
  · change x 1=y 1
    exact h2

theorem actual_noisy_reading_is_outside_the_two_dimensional_column_space :
    ¬∃z : Fin 2 → ℝ,rectangularH *ᵥ z=noisyY := by
  rintro ⟨z,h⟩
  have h0 := congrArg (fun v : Fin 3 → ℝ => v 0) h
  have h1 := congrArg (fun v : Fin 3 → ℝ => v 1) h
  have h2 := congrArg (fun v : Fin 3 → ℝ => v 2) h
  simp [rectangularH,noisyY,Matrix.mulVec,dotProduct,Fin.sum_univ_succ] at h0 h1 h2
  linarith

theorem actual_rectangular_residual_norm_is_the_sum_of_channel_squares (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    ‖actualResidual z‖^2 = CompleteFoundationsBook.sensorLoss (z 0) (z 1) := by
  rw [EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq]
  simp [actualResidual,PiLp.toLp_apply,rectangularH,noisyY,
    Matrix.mulVec,dotProduct,Fin.sum_univ_succ,CompleteFoundationsBook.sensorLoss]
  ring

theorem actual_rectangular_squared_residual_has_the_attained_unique_estimate (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    ‖actualResidual ![261/67,422/201]‖^2 ≤ ‖actualResidual z‖^2 ∧
    (‖actualResidual z‖^2=‖actualResidual ![261/67,422/201]‖^2 ↔ z=![261/67,422/201]) := by
  rw [actual_rectangular_residual_norm_is_the_sum_of_channel_squares,
    actual_rectangular_residual_norm_is_the_sum_of_channel_squares]
  have h := CompleteFoundationsBook.three_sensor_unique_optimum (z 0) (z 1)
  constructor
  · exact h.1
  · change CompleteFoundationsBook.sensorLoss (z 0) (z 1)=
      CompleteFoundationsBook.sensorLoss (261/67) (422/201) ↔ z=![261/67,422/201]
    rw [h.2]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h0,h1⟩
      ext i
      fin_cases i <;> simp [h0,h1]
    · intro hz
      rw [hz]
      simp

theorem actual_exact_fitting_does_not_identify_the_teaching_state :
    rectangularH *ᵥ (![5,2] : Fin 2 → ℝ)=![7,36/5,2] ∧
    rectangularH *ᵥ (![4,2] : Fin 2 → ℝ)+(![1,1,0] : Fin 3 → ℝ)=![7,36/5,2] ∧
    (point 5 2 : E)≠point 4 2 := by
  constructor
  · ext i
    fin_cases i <;> norm_num [rectangularH,Matrix.mulVec,dotProduct,Fin.sum_univ_succ]
  constructor
  · ext i
    fin_cases i <;> norm_num [rectangularH,Matrix.mulVec,dotProduct,Fin.sum_univ_succ]
  · intro h
    have h0 := congrArg (fun x : E => x 0) h
    norm_num [point] at h0

theorem actual_row_scaling_changes_the_true_squared_residual_weights
    {J : Type*} [Fintype J] (scale residual : J → ℝ) :
    ‖(WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => scale i*residual i) : EuclideanSpace ℝ J)‖^2 =
      ∑i,(scale i)^2*(residual i)^2 := by
  rw [EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq]
  simp only [PiLp.toLp_apply]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i hi
  ring

def unweightedCriterion (x : ℝ) : ℝ := x^2+(x-2)^2
def weightedCriterion (x : ℝ) : ℝ := 9*x^2+(x-2)^2

theorem actual_equal_weights_have_unique_minimum_one (x : ℝ) :
    unweightedCriterion 1 ≤ unweightedCriterion x ∧
    (unweightedCriterion x=unweightedCriterion 1 ↔ x=1) := by
  have he : unweightedCriterion x=unweightedCriterion 1+2*(x-1)^2 := by
    unfold unweightedCriterion
    ring
  constructor
  · nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x-1)]
  · rw [he]
    constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x-1)]

theorem actual_different_channel_weights_have_unique_minimum_one_fifth (x : ℝ) :
    weightedCriterion (1/5) ≤ weightedCriterion x ∧
    (weightedCriterion x=weightedCriterion (1/5) ↔ x=1/5) := by
  have he : weightedCriterion x=weightedCriterion (1/5)+10*(x-1/5)^2 := by
    unfold weightedCriterion
    ring
  constructor
  · nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x-1/5)]
  · rw [he]
    constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x-1/5)]

theorem actual_weight_choice_changes_the_estimate :
    (1 : ℝ)≠1/5 ∧ weightedCriterion (1/5)<weightedCriterion 1 ∧
      unweightedCriterion 1<unweightedCriterion (1/5) := by
  norm_num [weightedCriterion,unweightedCriterion]

def weakMeasurement (delta : ℝ) : E →L[ℝ] E :=
  CompleteFoundationsSpectralModels.applyMatrix !![delta,0;0,1]

theorem actual_invertible_weak_direction_has_large_state_error_with_arbitrarily_small_residual
    (epsilon M : ℝ) (hepsilon : 0<epsilon) (hM : 0<M) :
    ∃delta : ℝ,0<delta ∧ Function.Injective (weakMeasurement delta) ∧
      ‖point M 0‖=M ∧ ‖weakMeasurement delta (point M 0)‖=epsilon/2 ∧
      ‖weakMeasurement delta (point M 0)‖<epsilon := by
  let delta := epsilon/(2*M)
  have hd : 0<delta := div_pos hepsilon (mul_pos (by norm_num) hM)
  have ha (x : E) : weakMeasurement delta x=point (delta*x 0) (x 1) := by
    rw [weakMeasurement,CompleteFoundationsSpectralModels.matrix_coordinate_action]
    simp
  have hinj : Function.Injective (weakMeasurement delta) := by
    intro x y h
    rw [ha,ha] at h
    have h0 := congrArg (fun z : E => z 0) h
    have h1 := congrArg (fun z : E => z 1) h
    change delta*x 0=delta*y 0 at h0
    change x 1=y 1 at h1
    ext i
    fin_cases i
    · change x 0=y 0
      exact (mul_left_cancel₀ hd.ne' h0)
    · change x 1=y 1
      exact h1
  have hn : ‖point M 0‖=M := by
    have hs := norm_squared_coordinates (point M 0)
    change ‖point M 0‖^2=M^2+0^2 at hs
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (point M 0)]
  have hm : delta*M=epsilon/2 := by
    dsimp [delta]
    field_simp [ne_of_gt hM]
    <;> ring
  have hnorm : ‖weakMeasurement delta (point M 0)‖=epsilon/2 := by
    rw [ha]
    change ‖point (delta*M) 0‖=epsilon/2
    rw [hm]
    have hs := norm_squared_coordinates (point (epsilon/2) 0)
    change ‖point (epsilon/2) 0‖^2=(epsilon/2)^2+0^2 at hs
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (point (epsilon/2) 0)]
  exact ⟨delta,hd,hinj,hn,hnorm,by rw [hnorm];linarith⟩

def sumRow : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 2) ℝ := !![1,1]
def sumPlus : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 1) ℝ := !![1/2;1/2]
def moorePenrose {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
    (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (B : Matrix n m ℝ) : Prop :=
  A*B*A=A ∧ B*A*B=B ∧ (A*B)ᵀ=A*B ∧ (B*A)ᵀ=B*A

theorem actual_sum_row_moore_penrose_identities : moorePenrose sumRow sumPlus := by
  refine ⟨?_,?_,?_,?_⟩
  all_goals ext i j
  all_goals fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
    norm_num [sumRow,sumPlus,Matrix.mul_apply,Fin.sum_univ_succ]

theorem actual_sum_row_pseudoinverse_is_unique (B : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 1) ℝ)
    (hB : moorePenrose sumRow B) : B=sumPlus := by
  have h0 := congrArg (fun M : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 2) ℝ => M 0 0) hB.1
  have h1 := congrArg (fun M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ => M 0 1) hB.2.2.2
  simp [sumRow,Matrix.mul_apply,Matrix.vecMul,dotProduct,Fin.sum_univ_succ] at h0 h1
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [sumPlus] <;> linarith

theorem actual_pseudoinverse_of_sum_six_returns_three_three :
    sumPlus *ᵥ (![6] : Fin 1 → ℝ)=![3,3] := by
  ext i
  fin_cases i <;> norm_num [sumPlus,Matrix.mulVec,dotProduct,Fin.sum_univ_succ]

theorem actual_sum_solution_family_has_the_printed_squared_norm (t : ℝ) :
    ‖point (3+t) (3-t)‖^2=18+2*t^2 := by
  rw [norm_squared_coordinates]
  simp [point]
  ring

theorem actual_sum_minimum_length_is_unique_but_the_measurement_does_not_identify
    (x : E) (hx : x 0+x 1=6) :
    ‖point 3 3‖ ≤ ‖x‖ ∧ (‖x‖=‖point 3 3‖ ↔ x=point 3 3) ∧
    (3 : ℝ)+3=6 ∧ (4 : ℝ)+2=6 ∧ point 3 3≠point 4 2 := by
  have h := CompleteFoundationsBook.sum_measurement_unique_minimum (x 0) (x 1) hx
  have hn := norm_squared_coordinates x
  have hp : ‖point 3 3‖^2=18 := by rw [norm_squared_coordinates];norm_num [point]
  refine ⟨?_,?_,by norm_num,by norm_num,?_⟩
  · nlinarith [norm_nonneg x,norm_nonneg (point 3 3)]
  · constructor
    · intro he
      have hh : x 0=3 ∧ x 1=3 := h.2.mp (by rw [←hn,he,hp])
      ext i
      fin_cases i <;> simp [point,hh.1,hh.2]
    · rintro rfl
      rfl
  · intro he
    have hh := congrArg (fun z : E => z 0) he
    norm_num [point] at hh


theorem actual_rectangular_column_space_has_dimension_two :
    Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.range (Matrix.toLin' rectangularH))=2 := by
  have hi : Function.Injective (Matrix.toLin' rectangularH) := by
    intro x y h
    apply actual_rectangular_columns_are_independent
    simpa only [Matrix.toLin'_apply] using h
  simpa using LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj hi

theorem actual_sum_measurement_has_exactly_the_full_printed_vector_family (x : E) :
    x 0+x 1=6 ↔ ∃t : ℝ,x=point (3+t) (3-t) := by
  rw [CompleteFoundationsBook.sum_measurement_all_solutions]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨t,h0,h1⟩
    refine ⟨t,?_⟩
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> simp [point,h0,h1]
  · rintro ⟨t,rfl⟩
    exact ⟨t,by simp [point],by simp [point]⟩

end SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsResidualWeightingIdentification27

Noisy readings may fail to lie in its two-dimensional column space, so no displacement vector matches all of them exactly. Least squares chooses the estimate minimizing the sum of squared residuals, $\|H\hat z-y\|_2^2$. A residual is a mismatch in measurement space, not automatically a displacement error.

Equal residual weights assume that squared errors in the different channels are comparable for the decision being made. If one sensor has a much different error scale, scaling or weighting the rows may be appropriate, but that is an additional modeling choice. A small residual can also coexist with a large state error along a weakly observed direction. Checking residuals and checking sensitivity answer different questions.

With only the sum measurement $z_1+z_2=6$, a pseudoinverse returns $(3,3)$. That is the solution of smallest Euclidean length, because $\|(3+t,3-t)\|_2^2=18+2t^2$. The measurement did not establish equal displacements. Repair the conclusion by reporting the full solution family or by stating the extra criterion explicitly. A convenient unique estimate is not the same as uniquely determined physical quantities.

What to look for. Walkthrough: no real eigenvectors ($\rho=2$), yet two singular directions with $\sigma_1=2\sqrt2$; the power estimate climbs to $2.83$ from below. Symmetric PD: eigen- and singular vectors coincide, the level sets are ellipses with semi-axes $1/\sqrt{\lambda_i}$, Cholesky succeeds. Indefinite: hyperbolas; Cholesky fails at pivot 2 although all entries are positive. Singular PSD: the ellipse collapses to a segment (rank 1), level sets become lines. Nilpotent: $\rho(A)=0$ but $\|A\|_2=2$, and power iteration from $(1,0)\perp v_1$ breaks down at once: $(1,0)\in\mathrm{null}(A)$, so $A^\top A(1,0)=0$ and there is no next iterate (the readout says so). Rotation: $\sigma_1=\sigma_2=1$ (every direction is a dominant one, so $v_1$ is not unique), and $S=0.6I$ is PD although $A$ is not symmetric.

From the mathematics to a real decision

Two sensor channels do not automatically give two independent pieces of information. If both channels measure almost the same combination of unknown quantities, a small reading error can become a large reconstruction error. This chapter uses a constructed displacement fixture to connect linear systems, singular values, least squares and uncertainty geometry. Every displacement and sensor error below is hypothetical; the example is a teaching model for deciding what a calculation can support.

Learning objectives
  • Read matrix rows as measurements and columns as responses to individual unknowns.
  • Propagate a bounded measurement error through a linear reconstruction.
  • Distinguish a unique solution, a well-conditioned solution and a minimum-length convention.
  • Use residual orthogonality to check a least-squares estimate and state what it cannot verify.

A matrix is a measurement design

Let $z=(z_1,z_2)^\top$ contain two unknown fixture displacements, both in millimetres. A linear measurement model is $y=Hz+\eta$, where $y$ is the vector of sensor readings and $\eta$ is additive sensor error, also in millimetres. Each row of the dimensionless matrix $H$ describes one channel: it lists the coefficient multiplying each unknown displacement. Each column tells how all readings change when only one displacement increases by one millimetre.

To use the model, one assumes these coefficients are known and remain valid over the displacement range being studied. Calibration error in $H$ is a different uncertainty from additive error in $y$; the examples initially include only the latter. Solving the linear equations cannot establish that the measurement model itself is correct. It gives a conditional reconstruction from a stated model.

Suppose one channel measures the sum $z_1+z_2$ and another measures the difference $z_1-z_2$. Equal readings can then be explained by changes in different combinations. Adding and subtracting the channels separates these combinations. The matrix calculation is a compact record of that physical idea.

Worked example — Reconstruct displacements and carry the sensor bound

Set up. Take $H=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$ and readings $y=(6,2)^\top$ millimetres. First ignore additive error to compute an estimate $\hat z$. The equations are $\hat z_1+\hat z_2=6$ and $\hat z_1-\hat z_2=2$. Adding gives $2\hat z_1=8$; subtracting gives $2\hat z_2=4$. Thus $\hat z=(4,2)^\top$ millimetres.

Check the map. Multiplication gives $H\hat z=(6,2)^\top$. Also $H^\top H=2I$, where $I$ is the two-dimensional identity. Therefore $\|Hz\|_2^2=z^\top H^\top Hz=2\|z\|_2^2$: every direction stretches by $\sqrt2$. Both singular values are $\sqrt2$, so the spectral condition number is one. There is no preferred weak direction.

Restore uncertainty. With $|\eta_i|\le0.1$, the error in the estimate is $\hat z-z=H^{-1}\eta$, since $\hat z=H^{-1}y$ and $y=Hz+\eta$. Here:

$$\hat z-z=\frac12\begin{bmatrix}\eta_1+\eta_2\\\eta_1-\eta_2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \|\hat z-z\|_2=\frac{\|\eta\|_2}{\sqrt2}\le0.1\ \text{mm}.$$

Decide. If a hypothetical assembly requires $z_1\le4.15$ millimetres, its worst permitted value is $4.1$, so this upper-limit test passes. A requirement $z_1\le4.05$ would not be certified. The error set is a rotated square, not a square with independent reconstructed errors: attaining the largest error in the first displacement forces zero error in the second at the relevant sensor-error corners.

Find the direction the measurements barely see

A system can be invertible while giving fragile estimates. Replace the difference channel by another almost-sum channel. The rows now point in nearly the same direction. Increasing $z_1$ while decreasing $z_2$ leaves the first reading unchanged and changes the second only slightly. This is a weakly observed direction: a large displacement change produces a small measurement change.

The smallest singular value quantifies the weakest stretch. For an invertible square matrix, the largest amplification through its inverse is $1/\sigma_{\min}(H)$. The condition number $\sigma_{\max}(H)/\sigma_{\min}(H)$ compares the strongest and weakest stretches; it concerns relative sensitivity in Euclidean coordinates. It is not a universal absolute error bound without a measurement error size. Units and coordinate scaling must be chosen before interpreting that comparison.

Worked example — Transfer to nearly redundant sensors

Change the design. Let $H=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&1.1\end{bmatrix}$ and let the error-free readings be $(6,6.2)^\top$ millimetres. Subtraction gives $0.1z_2=0.2$, hence $z_2=2$ and $z_1=4$. The determinant $0.1$ is nonzero, so the solution is unique.

Inject a small permitted error. Perturb the readings by $\eta=(0.01,-0.01)^\top$. The new readings are $(6.01,6.19)^\top$. Their difference is $0.18$, so the reconstructed second displacement becomes $1.8$. Subtracting it from $6.01$ gives the first displacement $4.21$. The error is $(0.21,-0.2)^\top$, whose Euclidean length is $0.29$ millimetres, although each sensor changed by only $0.01$ millimetres.

Explain the sensitivity. Direct elimination gives $\Delta z_2=(\eta_2-\eta_1)/0.1$ and $\Delta z_1=11\eta_1-10\eta_2$. Opposite-sign errors are amplified by subtraction and division by the small row difference. Since this particular $H$ is symmetric positive definite, its singular values equal its positive eigenvalues:

$$\sigma_{\max,\min}=\frac{2.1\pm\sqrt{4.01}}2,\qquad \sigma_{\min}\approx0.04875,\qquad \kappa_2(H)\approx42.08.$$

Make a design decision. Exact solution of these equations cannot remove the sensitivity. A sensor observing a genuinely different direction, stronger sensor accuracy, or an additional justified prior constraint would change the information. Reporting more decimal places would not. Replacing $1.1$ by exactly $1$ would remove uniqueness altogether: both channels would report only the sum.

More measurements require a fitting criterion

Adding a third channel that directly measures $z_2$ gives a rectangular matrix. Noisy readings may fail to lie in its two-dimensional column space, so no displacement vector matches all of them exactly. Least squares chooses the estimate minimizing the sum of squared residuals, $\|H\hat z-y\|_2^2$. A residual is a mismatch in measurement space, not automatically a displacement error.

To derive the check without memorizing a derivative, perturb a candidate estimate by a small vector $tv$. Writing $r=H\hat z-y$, the squared residual becomes $\|r+tHv\|_2^2=\|r\|_2^2+2t v^\top H^\top r+t^2\|Hv\|_2^2$. A minimum cannot improve for either sign of sufficiently small $t$, so $H^\top r=0$. The residual is perpendicular to every possible modeled change in the readings. If $H$ has independent columns, $H^\top H$ is positive definite and this condition identifies a unique least-squares estimate.

Equal residual weights assume that squared errors in the different channels are comparable for the decision being made. If one sensor has a much different error scale, scaling or weighting the rows may be appropriate, but that is an additional modeling choice. A small residual can also coexist with a large state error along a weakly observed direction. Checking residuals and checking sensitivity answer different questions.

Common mistake — treating a convention as information

With only the sum measurement $z_1+z_2=6$, a pseudoinverse returns $(3,3)$. That is the solution of smallest Euclidean length, because $\|(3+t,3-t)\|_2^2=18+2t^2$. variable {V W : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [CompleteSpace V]
    [NormedAddCommGroup W] [InnerProductSpace ℝ W] [CompleteSpace W]

def loss (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x : V) : ℝ := ‖A x-y‖^2

theorem actual_residual_two_sided_perturbation_expansion
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x v : V) (t : ℝ) :
    loss A y (x+t • v) = loss A y x +
      2*t*inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v)+t^2*‖A v‖^2 := by
  have he : A (x+t • v)-y = (A x-y)+t • A v := by
    rw [map_add,map_smul]
    abel
  rw [loss,he,norm_add_sq_real]
  simp only [real_inner_smul_right,norm_smul,Real.norm_eq_abs,mul_pow,sq_abs,loss]
  ring

theorem actual_global_minimum_forces_every_residual_inner_product_zero
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x : V)
    (hmin : ∀z : V,loss A y x ≤ loss A y z) (v : V) :
    inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v) = 0 := by
  have hq : ∀t : ℝ,0 ≤ ‖A v‖^2*(t*t)+
      (2*inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v))*t+0 := by
    intro t
    have h := hmin (x+t • v)
    rw [actual_residual_two_sided_perturbation_expansion] at h
    nlinarith
  have hd := discrim_le_zero hq
  simp only [discrim,mul_zero,sub_zero] at hd
  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v))]

theorem actual_normal_equation_iff_residual_perpendicular_to_whole_range
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x : V) :
    A.adjoint (A x-y)=0 ↔ ∀v : V,inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v)=0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h v
    rw [← A.adjoint_inner_left v (A x-y),h,inner_zero_left]
  · intro h
    apply (inner_self_eq_zero (𝕜 := ℝ)).mp
    rw [A.adjoint_inner_left]
    exact h (A.adjoint (A x-y))

theorem actual_normal_equation_gives_exact_global_loss_difference
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x : V)
    (hx : A.adjoint (A x-y)=0) (z : V) :
    loss A y z = loss A y x + ‖A (z-x)‖^2 := by
  have ho := (actual_normal_equation_iff_residual_perpendicular_to_whole_range A y x).mp hx
  have he := actual_residual_two_sided_perturbation_expansion A y x (z-x) 1
  simp only [one_smul,add_sub_cancel,one_pow,mul_one,ho,mul_zero,add_zero] at he
  simpa using he

theorem actual_least_squares_global_minimum_iff_normal_equation
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x : V) :
    (∀z : V,loss A y x ≤ loss A y z) ↔ A.adjoint (A x-y)=0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    apply (actual_normal_equation_iff_residual_perpendicular_to_whole_range A y x).mpr
    exact actual_global_minimum_forces_every_residual_inner_product_zero A y x h
  · intro h z
    rw [actual_normal_equation_gives_exact_global_loss_difference A y x h z]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (sq_nonneg _)

theorem actual_independent_columns_gram_is_strictly_positive
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (hA : Function.Injective A) (v : V) (hv : v≠0) :
    0 < inner ℝ v (A.adjoint (A v)) := by
  rw [A.adjoint_inner_right,real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
  have hn : A v ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    apply hv
    apply hA
    simpa using h
  exact sq_pos_of_pos (norm_pos_iff.mpr hn)

theorem actual_independent_columns_make_the_normal_equation_solution_unique
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (hA : Function.Injective A) (y : W) (x : V)
    (hx : A.adjoint (A x-y)=0) (z : V) :
    loss A y z = loss A y x ↔ z=x := by
  rw [actual_normal_equation_gives_exact_global_loss_difference A y x hx z]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hs : ‖A (z-x)‖^2=0 := by linarith
    have hn : ‖A (z-x)‖=0 := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg (A (z-x))]
    have hz : A (z-x)=0 := norm_eq_zero.mp hn
    have hzx : z-x=0 := hA (by simpa using hz)
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp hzx
  · rintro rfl
    simp

theorem actual_finite_dimensional_independent_columns_have_one_attained_minimum
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (hA : Function.Injective A) (y : W) :
    ∃!x : V,∀z : V,loss A y x ≤ loss A y z := by
  have hinj : Function.Injective (A.adjoint.comp A).toLinearMap :=
    A.adjoint_comp_self_injective_iff.mpr hA
  have hsurj := LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective.mp hinj
  obtain ⟨x,hx⟩ := hsurj (A.adjoint y)
  have hn : A.adjoint (A x-y)=0 := by
    rw [map_sub]
    exact sub_eq_zero.mpr hx
  refine ⟨x,(actual_least_squares_global_minimum_iff_normal_equation A y x).mpr hn,?_⟩
  intro z hz
  apply (actual_independent_columns_make_the_normal_equation_solution_unique A hA y x hn z).mp
  exact le_antisymm (hz x)
    ((actual_least_squares_global_minimum_iff_normal_equation A y x).mpr hn z)

theorem actual_independent_matrix_columns_give_positive_definite_transpose_gram
    {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (H : Matrix m n ℝ) (hH : Function.Injective H.mulVec) :
    (H.transpose*H).PosDef := by
  have ht : H.conjTranspose=H.transpose := by
    ext i j
    simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_apply]
  rw [← ht]
  refine Matrix.PosDef.of_dotProduct_mulVec_pos (Matrix.isHermitian_conjTranspose_mul_self H) ?_
  intro x hx
  rw [← Matrix.mulVec_mulVec,Matrix.dotProduct_mulVec,Matrix.vecMul_conjTranspose,star_star]
  apply Matrix.dotProduct_star_self_pos_iff.mpr
  intro hz
  apply hx
  apply hH
  simpa using hz

theorem actual_residual_direction_derivative_follows_from_expansion
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x v : V) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => loss A y (x+t • v))
      (2*inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v)) 0 := by
  have h := ((hasDerivAt_const (0 : ℝ) (loss A y x)).add
    ((hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).const_mul (2*inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v)))).add
    (((hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).pow 2).const_mul (‖A v‖^2))
  convert h using 1
  · funext t
    change loss A y (x+t • v) = loss A y x + (2*inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v))*t + ‖A v‖^2*t^2
    rw [actual_residual_two_sided_perturbation_expansion]
    ring
  · norm_num

theorem actual_every_local_minimum_has_a_residual_perpendicular_to_whole_range
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x : V) (hx : IsLocalMin (loss A y) x) :
    ∀v : V,inner ℝ (A x-y) (A v)=0 := by
  intro v
  have hc : ContinuousAt (fun t : ℝ => x+t • v) 0 := by fun_prop
  have hl : IsLocalMin (loss A y) ((fun t : ℝ => x+t • v) 0) := by simpa using hx
  have hlocal : IsLocalMin (fun t : ℝ => loss A y (x+t • v)) 0 :=
    IsLocalMin.comp_continuous (g := fun t : ℝ => x+t • v) hl hc
  have hd := hlocal.hasDerivAt_eq_zero
    (actual_residual_direction_derivative_follows_from_expansion A y x v)
  linarith

theorem actual_local_least_squares_minimum_is_already_a_global_minimum
    (A : V →L[ℝ] W) (y : W) (x : V) (hx : IsLocalMin (loss A y) x) :
    ∀z : V,loss A y x ≤ loss A y z := by
  apply (actual_least_squares_global_minimum_iff_normal_equation A y x).mpr
  apply (actual_normal_equation_iff_residual_perpendicular_to_whole_range A y x).mpr
  exact actual_every_local_minimum_has_a_residual_perpendicular_to_whole_range A y x hx

theorem actual_rectangular_matrix_operator_action
    (H : Matrix m n ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixOperator H x = WithLp.toLp 2 (H *ᵥ (x : n → ℝ)) := by

    (H : Matrix m n ℝ) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ m) :
    (matrixOperator H).adjoint y = WithLp.toLp 2 (H.transpose *ᵥ (y : m → ℝ)) := by
  have ht : H.conjTranspose=H.transpose := by
    ext i j

    ←Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint,ht]
  rfl

    (H : Matrix m n ℝ) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ m) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :

    (H : Matrix m n ℝ) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ m) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :

  · intro h
    change WithLp.toLp 2 (H.transpose *ᵥ (H *ᵥ (x : n → ℝ)-(y : m → ℝ)))=0

    rfl
